display.purpose: House name in the dawn hero; inner page titles. Marcellus uppercase.

title.purpose: Service and house names under photographs.

lead.purpose: Owner's introduction and letter, display face in sentence case.

label.purpose: Units, hour names, legends, learn links.

cue-figure.purpose: Real figures from the owner's copy only.

shadows.name: key-lift
shadows.purpose: Primary button at rest; hover 0 16px 36px -14px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55).

shadows.name: floating-chrome
shadows.purpose: Day dial; its open cue list uses 0 24px 50px -20px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6).

shadows.name: inset-hairline
shadows.purpose: Ghost key, menu key, language tabs; hover to --ink.

shadows.name: phase-light
shadows.purpose: Edge vignette on every framed photograph.

shadows.name: horizon-glow
shadows.purpose: Dawn hero horizon line only; vane rim uses drop-shadow(0 0 1px rgb(255 214 190 / 0.95)) drop-shadow(0 0 22px rgb(240 168 162 / 0.55)).

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Entrances: reveal (0.9s, 28px rise), curtain lift (1.1s), photo settle (1.6s from 1.14x), menu.

motion.name: ease-smooth
motion.purpose: State changes: button press 160ms, chip slide 300ms, tabs 250ms, learn chevron 350ms.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Language tabs pill, cue list open.

motion.name: sky-crossfade
motion.value: opacity over 35% of viewport, next section from 100% to 65%

components.name: Horizon Rule
components.description: 1px hairline that glows in the hour's accent where title meets photo stage.

narrative.northStar: A Day at the Casale, Lit Like a Cyclorama
narrative.overview:
The whole site stands in front of one seamless, fixed sky. Every section declares the hour it belongs to (dawn, morning, noon, afternoon, sunset, night). As the next section rises past 65% of the viewport, its sky crossfades in over the current one, by opacity only. Text, rules, accents and photo plates all read from the lit hour, so one page shifts from cobalt dawn through white noon and ochre afternoon to terracotta sunset and cypress-black night. There are no fixed brand surfaces. The light is the surface.

The building materials come from the stage. Headlines are set in Roman capitals like an inscription. Real figures from the owner's copy (15 km, 50 m, 10 x 5 x 1.5 m) stand as condensed stencil numerals, like lighting cues. A thin horizon rule glows where sky meets photograph. The rooster weathervane is the only actor, and it is drawn as a mask so it takes whatever colour the hour gives it. The photographs are the stage below the horizon. The interface frames them with flat, near-square keys and hairlines, then steps back.

Density is generous and paced like a day: long section bands (112px to 160px vertical padding), big display headings, prose capped near 62ch, with staggered photo clusters instead of rows of equal cards.
keyCharacteristics: One fixed sky with six gradient layers that crossfade by opacity. Sections never paint their own backgrounds.
Six phase palettes (ink, soft, line, accent, on-accent, plate). Every colour on a page reads from the current phase.
Marcellus Roman capitals for headings, Hanken Grotesk for reading and labels, Saira Stencil for figures and button keys only.
Near-square stage-desk geometry (2px and 3px). The pill and the circle are reserved for the language switch and the sun.
Motion uses transform and opacity only, with expo-out easing. Every entrance has a reduced-motion and no-JS fallback.

rules.name: The Lit Hour Rule
rules.body: No component owns a colour. Pull every colour from the phase variables (`--ink`, `--soft`, `--line`, `--accent`, `--on-accent`, `--plate`) so it relights when the sky changes. Fixed overlay chrome (header, day dial) carries its own `data-phase`, which follows the lit section.

rules.name: The One Actor Rule
rules.body: Each hour has exactly one accent. Use it only for what acts or is current. Never use it as a decorative fill.

rules.name: The Real Figure Rule
rules.body: Stencil numerals carry only figures from the owner's own copy, such as distances, pool dimensions and room areas. Counts that are not measurements (bedrooms, guests) read as a plain line of soft body text.

rules.name: The Stencil Is For Figures Rule
rules.body: Labels are small caps in the text face for legibility. The stencil face appears only in cue figures and button keys.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: No backdrop-filter blur and no 3D. Translucency is a `color-mix` of the plate colour over the sky.

dos: **Do** give every section a `data-phase` and take every colour from the phase variables, so that it relights with the sky.
**Do** set headings in Marcellus uppercase at +0.05em, and keep the stencil for real figures and button keys.
**Do** frame photographs with the curtain frame and phase light, using 3px corners or full bleed.
**Do** animate only transform and opacity with expo-out easing (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) or (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)), and give every animation a reduced-motion and no-JS fallback.
**Do** keep the availability action one tap away: the hero key, then the header key (desktop) or the floating key (mobile).
donts: **Don't** paint section backgrounds. The sky is the only background.
**Don't** set invented or decorative numbers in stencil. No prices, ratings or sunrise times.
**Don't** lay out rooms or services as a row of equal cards, or open a page with a centred serif title over a drone photo.
**Don't** round keys or frames beyond 3px. Pills and circles belong only to the language switch, the dial and map pins.
